name: Angular Patterns
description: Angular — standalone components, signals, RxJS best practices, lazy loading, OnPush change detection
content:
# Angular Patterns

- Use standalone components by default — avoid `NgModule` declarations for new components
- Use Angular signals (`signal()`, `computed()`, `effect()`) for reactive state instead of manual change detection
- Apply `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` to all components — rely on immutable data and signal-based reactivity
- Use RxJS operators properly — always unsubscribe with `takeUntilDestroyed()`, `async` pipe, or explicit `unsubscribe` in `ngOnDestroy`
- Lazy-load feature routes with `loadComponent` and `loadChildren` to reduce initial bundle size
- Use typed reactive forms (`FormGroup`, `FormControl`) with proper validation — avoid template-driven forms for complex cases
- Inject dependencies with the `inject()` function in functional contexts — prefer it over constructor injection in guards and resolvers
- Separate smart (container) and dumb (presentational) components — dumb components use `@Input`/`@Output` only
- Use Angular's built-in `HttpClient` with interceptors for auth tokens, error handling, and request/response transforms
- Follow the Angular style guide — one component per file, feature-based folder structure, consistent naming conventions
